Subject: Private offer - drawdown cadence & SKU attribution question

Hi Ana / John,

Thanks again for running the private offer paperwork with GCP. I had a quick operational question as we stitch the drawdown schedule into Aurora's internal chargeback model. In the draft PO we received the committed spend is allocated across three SKUs (inference-standard, inference-burst, embedding-fast). Can you confirm whether GCP will break down monthly drawdowns by SKU on the invoice or if Aurora will receive a single combined redemption line item?

We want to align the monthly burn forecast with Aurora's internal finance tagging — if GCP provides SKU-level lines we can map directly to product teams, otherwise we need to generate a forecast to attach to your procurement calendar.

Attached: Private_Offer_Drawdown_Schedule.xlsx (proposed monthly cadence).

Next steps I propose:
- Aurora confirms preferred invoice breakdown (SKU-level vs aggregated)
- Redwood sends a 6-month forecast with expected token/embedding split for approvals
- GCP confirms any constraints for partial month redemptions or minimum draw amounts

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call this week to align.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: procurement@aurora-sys.com (Ana Vasquez)
To: connor.obrien@redwood.inference, marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Date: 2026-10-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer - drawdown cadence & SKU attribution question

Connor,

Thanks for the clarity and the attachment. Our finance team prefers SKU-level breakout on the invoice so we can allocate charges to the right product owners. Can GCP support line-item attribution for each SKU in the private offer redemption? If not, we'll need Redwood to provide a monthly forecast with the following fields: month, sku, estimated_units, estimated_cost, internal_charge_code.

Two quick constraints from Aurora:
- We run monthly close on the 2nd business day, so invoices and redemption reports need to land by the 3rd
- For the first 90 days we want a hard cap on burst consumption to protect against runaway spend (proposal: burst capped at 25% of monthly committed dollars)

Can GCP confirm the invoicing format? If the marketplace can't, can Redwood commit to the forecast report above?

Regards,
Ana Vasquez
Head of Procurement
Aurora Systems

Subject: RE: Private offer - drawdown cadence & SKU attribution question

Hi all,

Thanks for the note. GCP Marketplace private offers can surface SKU-level redemption lines, but it depends on how the offer is configured. Two important implementation details:

1) The private offer's fulfillment mapping must include separate SKUs for each usage type — we see a lot of sellers consolidate into a single usage SKU which aggregates at invoice time.
2) If you want SKU-level lines, the private offer needs to be created with per-SKU pricing and the billing plan set to "report per-usage SKU." That will produce distinct line items on the invoice.

We can support a 90-day burst cap as a contractual guardrail, but that needs to be encoded in the offer's redemption policy and the Marketplace team will enforce it at redemption time. There is a timing window for setting caps — it must be finalized before the first redemption.

I'll loop in the partner engineer if you want a short implementation walkthrough.

Regards,
Priya Malhotra
GCP Marketplace - Partner Sales

Attachments: Implementation_Note_SKU_Mapping.pdf (pdf)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.inference, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference

Ana / Connor —

Thanks everyone. Per Priya's note: Redwood can (and will) supply a monthly forecast report that matches Aurora's requested fields while we confirm the offer config with GCP. I attached the draft SOW and a 6-month forecast template filled with conservative estimates for the first three months (burst capped at 25% of committed dollars as requested).

Key asks for Aurora to approve so we can finalize the GCP offer:
- Approve the attached forecast (SOW_Aurora_Redwood_v1.docx)
- Confirm the internal_charge_code format (we used your "PRJ-XXXX" style in the spreadsheet)
- Sign-off on the 90-day burst cap and the associated fallback policy (we recommend automatic throttling, not hard-deny, so customer's app gets graceful degradation)

I'll update the HubSpot record once we have approval and then coordinate with GCP to ensure SKU-level lines are enabled.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Renewals & Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
